thread:
pagerduty-bot: PAGERDUTY ALERT: prefills causing GPU OOMs in cluster infer-prod-us-east-1. ~60% of gpu-pool-a containers restarted. Incident INC-2024-6789. Triggered at 2024-08-05T16:14:32Z.
Anya (oncall): ACK I'm on it, paging primary infra and eng-runtime. Will try to triage quickly.
Sam (sre): seeing a slow memory climb on the prefill path (/v1/chat/prefill). Not a single massive spike — memory increments over multiple long-prefill requests then boom OOM.
Lia (support): customer "Acorn" reported 5xx around 16:15 UTC for very long chat sessions. They said it started around 16:12.
Chris (eng-runtime): I have the logs tailing now. throwing a few snippets:
```
[2024-08-05T16:14:32Z] prefill request_id=abc123 user=acorn tokens=12500 mem_before_gpu=11.9GB mem_after_gpu=12.8GB cudaErrorOutOfMemory
[2024-08-05T16:14:32Z] container pid=4523 OOMKilled signal=9
[2024-08-05T16:14:35Z] prefill request_id=def456 user=beta tokens=9000 mem_before_gpu=10.1GB mem_after_gpu=11.0GB
```
Chris (eng-runtime): Also seeing logs where KV cache size doesn't drop after prefill completion for some sessions — entries stick around. Could be eviction not triggered on certain code paths (cancelled/cut streaming).
Anya (oncall): Ok immediate mitigations: 1) throttle prefill max tokens for hosted routes to reduce pressure, 2) enable a temporary stricter eviction window, 3) route heavy-context customers to fallback model family with lower mem (quantized).
Sam (sre): I can patch runtime env vars and restart pods. Proposing: PREFILL_MAX_TOKENS=4096 (was 16384), KV_EVICT_IMMEDIATELY=true, PREFILL_BATCH_MAX=8 -> lower batching for prefill.
Anya (oncall): do it, Sam. Lia please prepare a short customer update explaining temporary context truncation.
Lia (support): drafting: "We've detected GPU memory pressure caused by very long-context prefill requests and rolled a temporary mitigation. You may see truncated responses if your conversation exceeds ~4k tokens. We're working on a permanent fix and will update."
Sam (sre): applying changes now:
```
kubectl -n infer set env deploy/runtime PREFILL_MAX_TOKENS=4096 KV_EVICT_IMMEDIATELY=true PREFILL_BATCH_MAX=8
kubectl -n infer rollout restart deploy/runtime
```
deploy-bot: rollout started for deploy/runtime, 6 pods -> rolling restart.
Chris (eng-runtime): I'm also building a hotfix to explicitly clear KV on prefill finish/cancel. PR #4321 with a forced kvcache.clear() in the cancellation path. Will push image runtime:hotfix-20240805.
Anya (oncall): good. After rollout we need metrics: GPU mem headroom, Container restart rate, 5xx rate for /v1/chat routes, and customer errors for Acorn.
(5m later)
deploy-bot: rollout complete. 6/6 pods updated (runtime:hotfix-20240805 pending image swap on 2 pods).
Sam (sre): early telemetry: restart rate dropped from 0.6 -> 0.15 restarts/min in the pool. 5xx rate for prefill path down by ~70%. GPU mem growth still visible on two pods but slower.
Chris (eng-runtime): hotfix image pushed. I'll trigger a rolling restart to pick it up on remaining pods.
```
kubectl -n infer set image deploy/runtime runtime=registry.redwood/runtime:hotfix-20240805
kubectl -n infer rollout status deploy/runtime
```
Sam (sre): restarted with hotfix image. Observing that KV entries are being cleared after prefill now in debug traces.
Chris (eng-runtime): I instrumented an internal metric kvcache.size_per_session and saw several sessions that previously stayed at ~1.6M entries now drop to ~0 after completion. Looks promising.
Lia (support): sent update to Acorn. They replied they saw partial degradation but appreciate proactive communication. No revenue-impacting calls yet but they asked for ETA on permanent fix.
Anya (oncall): Customer impact: limited to customers sending very large prefill contexts (>8k tokens), about 12 customers saw elevated errors, highest impact was Acorn with ~120 failed requests. No billing anomalies reported.
Sam (sre): remaining to-dos before we close pager: 1) run canary longer (2 hours) with increased sampling for long-context requests 2) roll a test that reproduces leak locally (we have a failing script) 3) follow-up postmortem owner -> Chris.
Chris (eng-runtime): I own the postmortem and the proper fix (ensure eviction on all code paths + add automated regression test for long-prefill lifecycle). PR linked: #4321, will add unit + integration tests.
Anya (oncall): handing off monitoring to Chris (night oncall) at 18:00 UTC. Key checks for night: watch gpu-pool-a restart rate, kvcache.size_per_session, and error rate for /v1/chat/prefill. Pager duty escalation policy: if restarts/min > 0.2 or 5xx > 1% re-escalate to infra lead.
Chris (eng-runtime): ack, taking over. I'll keep the temporary PREFILL_MAX_TOKENS=4096 until a safer rollout of the full fix. Will coordinate with Sam if we need to scale the pool back up or cordon nodes.
Lia (support): I'll follow up with affected customers with timeline and offer a meeting if needed.
Anya (oncall): thanks team. Postmortem to be scheduled; initial blameless summary: long-context prefill flows were not releasing GPU KV cache on cancellation/stream termination, enabling slow memory accumulation that triggered OOMs under certain traffic mix. Hotfix mitigated immediate issue.
Chris (eng-runtime): adding follow-up action items to the issue: instrument more detailed GPU allocation traces, add regression harness for long prefill + cancellation, consider server-side prefill trimming and user-visible warnings.
Sam (sre): leaving a short runbook note for oncall: "If prefills cause GPU OOMs: 1) set PREFILL_MAX_TOKENS=4096 2) set KV_EVICT_IMMEDIATELY=true 3) rollout runtime hotfix image 4) monitor restart rate and kvcache.size_per_session."
Anya (oncall): closing pager for now, monitoring continues with handoff. Will reopen if regressions. :thumbsup:
